content_md:
Great idea from [Sean Stevenson's talk](https://protocol-institute.org/events/protocol-symposium-2026/#p-73) at Protocol Symposium -- the test of New Nature should be that there is nobody to appeal to.

Which sends me back to Paul Ford's [cult classic "Why wasn't I consulted"](https://www.ftrain.com/wwic) -- the argument that the web is fundamentally a customer service medium, and that WWIC is the fundamental question of the internet, the thing every comment section and pull request and reply-guy is really asking. The two ideas are the same idea from opposite ends: the web was built to make everyone feel consultable, and New Nature is what's left when there's no longer anyone on the other end of the complaint.
